question: How, in Berger's view, does advertising work on the people who see it?
answer: By selling envy of ourselves. An advert shows a future self, transformed by a product and envied by others, and so makes us dissatisfied with our present life. Berger called this publicity, and argued that it borrowed the language of oil painting: the same gleaming surfaces, now promising a life we don't yet have.
move: Notice when an ad sells a better you rather than a thing.
simply: Ads don't just sell shampoo; they show a happier, envied you. To get there, they first make you feel your life isn't quite enough.
why: Spotting the future you in an ad weakens its pull, and helps you decide whether you want the thing or the feeling it promises.
